question: Intermediate syndrome in organophosphate poisoning typically occurs 24–96 hours after the cholinergic crisis has resolved, and presents with proximal limb weakness, neck flexor weakness, and respiratory failure — requiring ventilatory support.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Intermediate syndrome occurs 24–96 hours after cholinergic crisis resolution — a critical trap because the patient appears to be recovering. The weakness of proximal limbs, neck flexors, and respiratory muscles can cause sudden respiratory arrest. Patients must be kept under observation even when they appear clinically stable.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Intermediate syndrome (Senanayake-Karalliedde syndrome) is a delayed neurotoxic complication that appears AFTER the cholinergic crisis has resolved (day 1–4), when the family and team may think the patient has recovered. It is thought to result from down-regulation of nicotinic receptors. There is no specific treatment other than respiratory support.
